item.description:
# What's New in TablePro 0.87.0-beta.2
### Added
- PostgreSQL notices such as RAISE NOTICE show in the Output view, and a plan from EXPLAIN ANALYZE gains Output too. ([#4061](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4061)) - Export Results… has a keyboard shortcut, ⌥⇧⌘E, which you can change in Settings > Keyboard. ([#4066](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4066)) - The tablepro command lists databases, schemas and tables, describes and exports tables, and reports its status. ([#4145](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4145)) - tablepro completion prints a completion script for zsh, bash and fish. ([#4145](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4145)) - tablepro pair and tablepro unpair pair the command with TablePro or revoke its token. ([#4145](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4145)) - Table Health exports findings to CSV, Excel, JSON and other formats, copies them, and saves every fix as one script. ([#4167](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4167)) - Table Health finds reclaimable space on MySQL and MariaDB. ([#4167](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4167)) - Table Health marks new findings, keeps resolved ones and lets you ignore a finding, per database. ([#4167](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4167)) - The get_table_health MCP tool returns Table Health findings to a connected client. ([#4167](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4167)) - Table Health checks redundant and invalid indexes, values near their limit, transaction ID age and stale statistics. ([#4167](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4167)) - Redshift AWS IAM sign-in accepts a custom domain name as Host. ([#4183](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4183)) - AWS IAM connections to Amazon RDS accept a custom CNAME as Host and follow it to the RDS endpoint on every connect. ([#4183](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4183)) - Meta (Muse Spark, Muse Wonder, Muse Ember) is an AI provider in Add Provider, with its Base URL filled in. ([#4191](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4191)) - PostgreSQL connections set to Verify Identity check the server against this Mac's trusted roots without a CA file. ([#4200](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4200)) - Color values by type in Settings > Data colors strings, numbers, dates, binary, JSON, UUID and enum values. ([#4205](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4205)) - A Values section in the Theme Editor sets the NULL, boolean and per-type value colors. ([#4205](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4205)) - Autocomplete offers join conditions from foreign keys right after the ON of a join. ([#4210](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4210)) - The MCP Activity Log shows and filters by the client that made each call. ([#4211](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4211)) - Connect a Client lists 21 AI clients, including Codex and VS Code, sets most up in one click and says when one connects. ([#4211](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4211)) - The ER diagram's Add Foreign Key sheet builds keys over several columns. ([#4214](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4214)) - Manual Commit keeps a connection's changes in a transaction until you commit or roll back. ([#4214](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4214)) - The sidebar lists MySQL and MariaDB events and PostgreSQL extensions, and opens their DDL. ([#4214](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4214)) - Query tabs keep earlier versions of their text, listed under File > Revert To. ([#4214](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4214)) - A table tab can refresh itself on an interval, set from its status bar or Database > Auto Refresh. ([#4214](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4214)) - Always Allow grants for assistant tools can be removed with Forget under AI Policy in the connection form. ([#4219](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4219)) - Settings > Data > Results kept per run limits how many results with rows a run keeps. ([#4246](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4246)) - SQL import and the query editor load the rows of a PostgreSQL COPY ... FROM STDIN, as psql sends them. ([#4255](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4255))
### Changed
- On iOS, usage data goes to PostHog instead of TablePro's server, and only after you choose Share Usage Data. ([#4058](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4058)) - tablepro exits 2 for a target that is neither a URL nor a file; open a file named like a command with tablepro open. ([#4145](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4145)) - SQL passed to tablepro query that starts with a dash now goes after --. ([#4145](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4145)) - tablepro opens files and links in the TablePro it ships in, and a hidden connection exits 2 like an unknown one. ([#4145](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4145)) - With Reduce Transparency on, themes now color the sidebar and inspector on macOS 26 and later. ([#4153](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4153)) - Table Health opens one tab per database and stays on it when the sidebar switches database. ([#4167](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4167)) - Run All shows statements that return no rows as one result, and keeps the last 100 results that return rows. ([#4200](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4200)) - On iPad, every window of a connection now shows Reconnecting or Lost at the same time. ([#4201](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4201)) - Bundled palette themes like Dracula and Nord color each value type, and booleans and values reach 4.5:1 on every row. ([#4205](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4205)) - Edited cells in Dracula and Nord use a lighter tint, so values stay readable on them. ([#4207](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4207)) - Themes that set Values colors, copies of built-in themes included, sync only to Macs on this version or later. ([#4207](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4207)) - Query tabs on Trino, Neo4j and similar drivers no longer read every table's columns up front. ([#4209](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4209)) - PostgreSQL connections open with five fewer round trips, so the sidebar lists tables sooner after a connect. ([#4209](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4209)) - AI provider and MCP client lists show each brand's logo instead of a generic symbol. ([#4211](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4211)) - Queries start sooner: running one no longer rewrites the whole execution log first. ([#4212](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4212)) - Copilot's schema context covers up to Max schema tables tables, the ones the current statement names first. ([#4218](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4218)) - A connection on an SSH profile asks once more before it signs in with this Mac's credentials or environment variables. ([#4222](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4222)) - Reset All Settings keeps AI providers, their API keys and the Enable AI Features switch. ([#4222](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4222)) - Large iOS query results use less memory, so more rows fit before the app stops at its memory limit. ([#4228](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4228)) - Returning to the iOS app syncs with iCloud at most once a minute. ([#4228](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4228)) - Opening a table on iOS shows its rows before the row count finishes, and sorting no longer counts the table again. ([#4228](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4228)) - On iOS, a PostgreSQL connection opens straight into the database and schema you last used. ([#4228](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4228)) - The iOS app starts faster: it no longer rebuilds Spotlight entries, widgets and Shortcuts at every launch. ([#4228](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4228)) - Switching back to TablePro syncs with iCloud at most once a minute. ([#4229](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4229)) - A theme edited in Finder or another app loads as soon as it is saved. ([#4229](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4229)) - Opening a remote database file over SFTP downloads it several times faster on high-latency links. ([#4229](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4229)) - TablePro and its plugins are smaller to download and install. ([#4233](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4233)) - MySQL, MariaDB, TiDB and OceanBase count an UPDATE's matched rows as affected, unchanged rows included. ([#4242](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4242)) - Read-Only blocks a query that calls a function which may change data, and names the level that runs it. ([#4244](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4244)) - An AI agent's statement over an open Teradata transaction is refused, since a failure would roll it all back. ([#4246](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4246)) - A Teradata script that starts with BT runs as its own transaction instead of inside one TablePro opens. ([#4246](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4246)) - Closing, disconnecting, quitting or relaunching with an open transaction now offers Commit as well as Roll Back. ([#4247](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4247)) - On iOS, reopening a MySQL, MariaDB or TiDB connection on the database you last used takes fewer round trips. ([#4252](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4252)) - iOS Read-Only runs PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB queries in a read-only transaction, so the server refuses their writes. ([#4257](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4257)) - Read-Only and Edit mode treat Redis module and new data-type reads, and Elasticsearch POST reads, as reads. ([#4260](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4260)) - Deleting one document, row or key by its ID is a write, so AI Edit mode and MCP's execute_query can run it. ([#4262](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4262)) - Read-Only runs Oracle MATCH_RECOGNIZE queries that use PREV, NEXT, FIRST, LAST, CLASSIFIER or MATCH_NUMBER. ([#4262](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4262)) - The SQL import progress bar follows how much of the file has been read, so it moves while a large COPY block loads. ([#4263](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4263)) - With iCloud sync on, changes from your other devices arrive within seconds while TablePro runs, in the background too. ([#4266](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4266)) - On iOS, changes from your other devices arrive within seconds while the app is open or iOS wakes it. ([#4266](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4266))
### Fixed
- Oracle output from a grid save, Commit or an AI statement showed under the next statement run from the editor. ([#4061](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4061)) - The Restore Previous Values toolbar button ignored a shortcut assigned to it in Settings > Keyboard. ([#4066](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4066)) - A database or schema's Export… in the sidebar showed ⇧⌘E, which exports the selected tables instead. ([#4066](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4066)) - Settings offered a tablepro link line that broke once TablePro left its disk image. ([#4145](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4145)) - tablepro --help and tablepro --version opened TablePro instead of printing help or the version. ([#4145](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4145)) - tablepro query with TablePro closed could start another copy of TablePro, or the iPad app, and then time out. ([#4145](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4145)) - Revoking an MCP token showed it as revoked even when TablePro could not save the change. ([#4145](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4145)) - Bars in the inspector lost their background under a theme on macOS 13 to 15. ([#4153](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4153)) - The license notice over Charts and Query Insights covered a themed window in system gray with Reduce Transparency on. ([#4153](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4153)) - Filter bar rows no longer center or drift out of line when a value is a pop-up, Between or Raw SQL. ([#4164](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4164)) - Table Health reported a PostgreSQL standby's activity counters and objects an extension owns. ([#4167](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4167)) - Pasting spreadsheet rows whose first cell is empty shifted every value one column left. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - An error sent mid-stream by an OpenAI-compatible or Gemini provider ended the reply silently. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Query parameters mistook Snowflake paths, array slices or ClickHouse typed slots for :name parameters. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - A SQL dump of a MySQL BIT column restored different values than the table held. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Saving a connection deleted its API token, TOTP secret or key passphrase when the Keychain could not be read. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Pasting or bulk-editing tens of thousands of rows froze the window for many seconds. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Parquet export wrote NULL for values that did not fit the column type, with no warning. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - A DuckDB export or table copy of more than 5,000,000 rows stopped at 5,000,000 and reported success. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Running a query over an edited result discarded the unsaved edits without asking. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Editing a MySQL or MariaDB BIT cell saved the wrong value: 5 was stored as 53. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - A long Snowflake statement was run a second time when the session expired while it ran. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Kafka topics and SurrealDB tables were browsed with a generic SQL SELECT instead of the driver's own query. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - A failed trigger edit could leave the trigger dropped with only a syntax error shown. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - One unreadable saved MCP token, or a failed keychain read, removed every paired client's token. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Items deleted on another Mac while their sync category was off stayed here and could come back everywhere. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - A transaction opened in a tab on another PostgreSQL database was silently rolled back after a few minutes. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - XLSX export turned text such as 1E5 or Infinity into numbers and lost digits of long ids. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Editing a Redis string value in the grid removed the key's TTL. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - A save could fail on a unique constraint because edits ran before earlier deletes. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Format Query split PostgreSQL operators such as pgvector's <#> or pg_trgm's <%. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Exporting an empty PostgreSQL table to CSV with field names wrote no header line. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Renaming an etcd key or adding one overwrote an existing key, and a rename took two separate steps. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Parquet export wrote wrong bytes for binary values and NULL for an empty one. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Copying a PostgreSQL text array into a JSON column wrote invalid JSON or turned strings into numbers. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Rebuilding a SQLite table with a transaction open in the editor deleted its child rows. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Keyword casing rewrote words inside string literals and in non-SQL editors such as MongoDB. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - After a dropped connection reconnected, statements ran outside the transaction that was lost, with no error. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Saving a password failed silently when the Keychain held both a synced and a local copy for the connection. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Edits left on a background tab were reapplied to a different result that arrived while it was hidden. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Adding an Elasticsearch row with an _id that exists replaced the existing document. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Renaming a Redis key or adding a string key overwrote an existing key of that name. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - A query approved in Safe Mode after switching tabs ran in the newly selected tab's database. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Copy DDL and SQL export recreated a PostgreSQL partitioned or unlogged table as a plain table. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Reopening a closed connection from a deeplink or history replaced its saved tabs with one tab. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Editing a MySQL or MariaDB trigger dropped it and ran its body as a statement. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - A write that outlasted the MCP or assistant timeout was reported as failed although it was applied. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - An outside MCP server with long or dotted tool names made every chat request on its connections fail. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Format Query put spaces around the @ of a MySQL account name or quoted user variable. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - A Snowflake statement still running after 45 minutes was reported as failed but kept running on the server. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Choosing Save on a second closing tab while the first was still saving left the first tab unclosable. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Editing a string in an untyped SurrealDB field to text that looks like a number changed its type. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - CSV import silently dropped extra fields. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - A structure save that failed part way on MySQL left edits staged that could not be saved again. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Deleting a row with unsaved edits could delete a different row, or none. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Stopping the assistant during a tool call broke the conversation; every later message failed. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Editing a field inside an Elasticsearch object left the old value in the document beside the new one. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Shortcuts Add Rows inserted empty CSV cells as empty strings instead of NULL or the column default. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Editing a MongoDB string field to text that looks like a number or boolean changed its type. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - A DuckDB query over a very large result held every row in memory twice before showing the first page. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Cmd+Return right after typing in a very large script ran the text from before the last keystrokes. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Redoing a cell edit on a row with another unsaved edit showed the value but never saved it. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - A sidebar command on another database's table ran on the current database when the switch failed. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Saving, switching tabs during the Safe Mode prompt, then approving wiped the other tab's edits. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - On macOS 27, clicking a row in a list or table no longer leaves its selection grey and the arrow keys going elsewhere. ([#4175](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4175)) - The host, attached database and extension lists in the connection form no longer hide the rows that do not fit. ([#4175](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4175)) - Return and Delete on a selected row in the Welcome window, Favorites and the connections strip no longer do nothing. ([#4175](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4175)) - A PostgreSQL query on iOS hung for about two hours when the network dropped its reply. ([#4177](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4177)) - Stop on iOS left a MySQL statement running on the server, which then committed it. ([#4177](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4177)) - A password saved on iOS while Sync Passwords was off went unused once Sync Passwords was turned back on. ([#4177](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4177)) - Switching apps on iOS with a DuckDB transaction open rolled it back without any message. ([#4177](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4177)) - MySQL statements on iOS that ran past 30 seconds failed while the server kept running and committed them. ([#4177](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4177)) - Saving a password on iOS with Sync Passwords off deleted the iCloud Keychain copy your other devices use. ([#4177](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4177)) - A MySQL or MariaDB query with no query timeout hung for about two hours when the network dropped its reply. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - Reading a SQLite full-text search table over MCP or from the assistant failed with authorization denied. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - Switching databases on a connection that reconnects to switch rolled back an open transaction without asking. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - Items deleted on another Mac came back after iCloud sync had to download everything again. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - Saving a connection rewrote passwords you did not change, overwriting a newer one saved on another device. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - A password saved while Sync Passwords was off went unused once Sync Passwords was turned back on. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - Claude Agent asked for MCP access to the chat's connection on every message at Ask Once. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - A structure save or column reorder that failed part way did not say which changes were already applied. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - Saving, closing or switching tabs right after typing in a very large script lost the last keystrokes. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - Importing, copying or syncing rows into a MySQL or MariaDB BIT column stored the wrong value: 5 became 53. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - Adding a Redis hash, list, set or sorted set key in the grid wrote into an existing key of that name. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - Editing a SurrealDB field that held both strings and numbers changed the edited value's type. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - Pasting spreadsheet rows with empty cells wrote NULL instead of the column's default value. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - A MySQL result on iOS that exactly filled the row cap said more rows were left out. ([#4179](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4179)) - The query timeout on iOS was ignored on PostgreSQL, Redshift and Oracle, and as a lock timeout on SQL Server. ([#4179](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4179)) - Text over 4 KB in a SQL Server, Oracle or DuckDB table on iOS could not be loaded in full, edited or copied. ([#4179](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4179)) - After a low-memory trim on iOS, the data browser's page range named rows it no longer showed. ([#4179](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4179)) - A large MySQL or SQL Server query on iOS kept downloading every remaining row after the row cap was reached. ([#4179](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4179)) - Typing in the row inspector after Fetch All on a large result lagged on every key. ([#4181](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4181)) - Column suggestions before FROM were slow to appear in schemas with many tables. ([#4181](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4181)) - Exporting a large Oracle table was far slower than the same export from other databases. ([#4181](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4181)) - Exporting more than 5,000,000 rows from SAP HANA wrote only the first 5,000,000 and reported success. ([#4181](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4181)) - Typing or moving the caret near the end of a long SQL script lagged while the current statement was highlighted. ([#4181](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4181)) - Refreshing many databases or schemas at once could open more server connections than the server allows. ([#4181](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4181)) - AI chat could read foreign keys for every table in a large schema on Snowflake, Trino, ClickHouse and others. ([#4181](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4181)) - Stopping an export from SAP HANA, Teradata, InfluxDB, Cloudflare R2 SQL or Memcached left its query running. ([#4181](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4181)) - The app froze during the first iCloud sync of a large connection library. ([#4181](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4181)) - Browsing, filtering or exporting a large etcd prefix downloaded every key and value at once. ([#4181](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4181)) - Run All on a script with thousands of statements froze the window and its result chooser. ([#4226](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4226)) - Pasting CSV removed the spaces inside quoted fields. ([#4226](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4226)) - Cmd+Z after Undo Delete on the row menu deleted the row again. ([#4226](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4226)) - Editing a formatted JSON value in the row inspector or the JSON editor saved it on one line. ([#4226](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4226)) - Restore Previous Values overwrote changes made to a row after the restore was reviewed. ([#4226](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4226)) - Duplicate on the row menu copied only the first of the selected rows. ([#4226](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4226)) - A structure save that stopped part way lost a staged drop and re-add of a column with the same name. ([#4226](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4226)) - Undoing a cell typed back to its value kept Restore Previous Values from bringing the old value back. ([#4226](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4226)) - Deleting more than 100 rows in one save failed part way on Cloudflare D1. ([#4226](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4226)) - Copying, comparing or exporting a large SQLite, Oracle, Teradata, Cassandra or cloud table held all of it in memory. ([#4227](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4227)) - Going past the last page of an iOS table before its row count arrived showed it as empty with a wrong total. ([#4228](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4228)) - Share Results and Copy Results on iOS froze the screen while they formatted a large result. ([#4228](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4228)) - Switching schema on iOS kept the previous schema's row count in the table pager. ([#4228](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4228)) - The Server Dashboard kept querying the server while its window was minimized, hidden or covered. ([#4229](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4229)) - An open SSH tunnel woke the Mac five times a second while TablePro sat idle. ([#4229](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4229)) - Each switch back to TablePro re-read every theme file and ran Git in each linked SQL folder. ([#4229](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4229)) - Snowflake leaked two network sessions each time a pooled connection opened. ([#4229](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4229)) - Every write another app made to a SQLite file reloaded the sidebar, even when the schema stayed the same. ([#4229](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4229)) - Saving any file in a linked SQL folder re-read every SQL file in it. ([#4229](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4229)) - A connection with a credential profile signed in without the profile's credentials when it used a tunnel. ([#4230](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4230)) - A refused SQL Server login showed a generic message instead of the server's reason. ([#4230](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4230)) - A Vault database role leased a new user on every sign-in, so a database slow to load users never accepted one. ([#4230](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4230)) - Quitting TablePro left every Vault database lease alive until it expired. ([#4230](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4230)) - Scrolling a result with large binary values stuttered. ([#4231](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4231)) - An ER diagram with hundreds of related tables took seconds to open, reset its layout or switch to Compact Mode. ([#4231](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4231)) - Moving from row to row with the inspector open was slow. ([#4231](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4231)) - Vim mode `dl`, `dh` and `cl` did nothing and left the operator waiting for the next key. ([#4236](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4236)) - An unquoted `begin` column in a one-statement MySQL procedure or event swallowed the rest of the script. ([#4236](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4236)) - Vim mode commands such as `x`, `r`, `h` and `l` split emoji and accented letters, and `f` with an emoji closed the app. ([#4236](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4236)) - Remove Invisible Characters changed the text in a string that followed a non-breaking or zero-width space. ([#4240](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4240)) - Saving an edit that matched no row reported success on MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, Oracle, Snowflake and Dameng. ([#4242](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4242)) - INSERT OVERWRITE, which empties the table first, was not treated as a destructive statement. ([#4244](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4244)) - Fetch All ran its query again without Safe Mode's check, so a level raised since the first run did not apply. ([#4244](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4244)) - An Always Allow grant let the assistant's query tool run on a Read-Only connection. ([#4244](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4244)) - An Elasticsearch export could leave out the documents of a shard that stopped answering, without an error. ([#4245](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4245)) - Copying, comparing or exporting a large Elasticsearch, Trino or MongoDB table held the whole table in memory. ([#4245](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4245)) - An MCP client's insert_rows reply never said that Manual Commit held the inserted rows. ([#4246](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4246)) - Tabbing through a binary field in the inspector without changing it marked the row as edited. ([#4246](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4246)) - Moving from row to row with the inspector open was slow with text, JSON, binary, image or geometry fields. ([#4246](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4246)) - On Teradata, saving two staged table drops failed, and Truncate sent a TRUNCATE statement Teradata does not have. ([#4247](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4247)) - A TablePro opened only to serve MCP kept running after MCP refused it. ([#4247](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4247)) - On Teradata, Run All failed on the statement after a DDL statement instead of stopping and asking you to commit. ([#4247](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4247)) - On Teradata ANSI sessions, structure edits, new tables, renames and drops were left uncommitted and could be lost. ([#4247](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4247)) - On Teradata, every statement after an uncommitted change was refused, a typed COMMIT included. ([#4247](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4247)) - Closing a connection under Manual Commit rolled back the edits you had just chosen to save. ([#4247](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4247)) - An SSH tunnel could stall every connection through it after a keep-alive met a full network buffer. ([#4248](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4248)) - A connection through an SSH tunnel could wait half a second for a reply while others were open. ([#4248](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4248)) - An open SSH tunnel woke TablePro twice a second for each connection and kept macOS from napping it. ([#4248](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4248)) - A SQLite over SSH connection set to open the database on the server never connected. ([#4249](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4249)) - Remove Invisible Characters left a non-ASCII space between the two parts of a PostgreSQL string, so the query failed. ([#4254](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4254)) - A MySQL routine with a `SET` or `IF` body naming a `begin` column swallowed the rest of the script on Run All. ([#4254](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4254)) - An etcd del with a range end or --from-key deleted only its first key. ([#4262](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4262)) - Deleting a Weaviate row in the grid also deleted objects with the same ID in other collections. ([#4262](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4262)) - Read-Only failed every query on MySQL before 5.6.5 and MariaDB before 10.0. ([#4264](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4264)) - Read-Only refused every query while a transaction was open, as on MySQL and MariaDB with autocommit off. ([#4264](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4264)) - TablePro could quit when the SQLite session on an SSH server ended while its connection stayed open. ([#4265](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4265)) - Copying, comparing or exporting a large table from a SQLite file on an SSH server held the whole table in memory. ([#4265](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4265)) - A query on a SQLite file on an SSH server could wait forever after the session on the server ended. ([#4265](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4265)) - Copying, comparing or exporting a SQLite or libSQL table kept other programs from writing the file until it ended. ([#4278](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4278)) - Importing a large SQL file held memory the size of the file while counting its statements or loading COPY rows. ([#4279](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4279)) - A read error while previewing or importing a SQL file quit TablePro instead of failing the import. ([#4279](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4279))
### Security
- tablepro export printed control codes stored in the database to the terminal, where they could run. ([#4145](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4145)) - The tablepro command and the MCP bridge could send their token to a program that replaced TablePro's socket. ([#4145](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4145)) - A Local only connection's newly saved passwords and keys still synced through iCloud Keychain. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - MCP argument completion listed a connection's databases and tables to a client that was not approved for it. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Deleting the connections.json tag file let an edited connection list run its password and tunnel commands. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Claude Agent could reach every saved connection through MCP instead of only the one the chat is on. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - MCP clients and the AI assistant could read masked values through a renamed column, a query plan or an error message. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - When the saved SSH host keys could not be read, a server whose key had changed was offered as a new server to trust. ([#4179](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4179)) - A shared connection could send an AWS IAM token to its author's server through a host like 127.0.0.1.example.com. ([#4183](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4183)) - A shared Elasticsearch, Kafka or MongoDB connection could mint an AWS IAM token on this Mac and send it to its servers. ([#4183](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4183)) - A plugin could load with any valid signature when TablePro's signing requirement failed to build. ([#4184](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4184)) - Another app on the Mac could take the IPv6 side of a sign-in callback port and receive the browser's redirect. ([#4184](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4184)) - A connection deleted on another device left its passwords and other secrets in this Mac's Keychain. ([#4184](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4184)) - Plugin secure fields could stay in plain text in connections.json after the upgrade that moves them to the Keychain. ([#4184](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4184)) - Browsing a Memcached cache with a key holding a line break could run a second command on the server. ([#4190](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4190)) - Marking a connection Local only left its passwords in iCloud Keychain on your other devices. ([#4200](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4200)) - Deleting a connection on iOS left its decrypted client private key in a file on the device. ([#4215](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4215)) - Read-Only Safe Mode ran a query that called a function which writes data. ([#4219](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4219)) - MCP clients could read the query history and tabs of connections the user had denied or never approved. ([#4219](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4219)) - Claude Agent could run queries and read rows in Ask mode. ([#4219](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4219)) - An MCP client could read files through a DuckDB table function or a file name used as a table. ([#4219](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4219)) - The assistant's list_connections sent every saved connection's host and database to the AI provider. ([#4219](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4219)) - Sign-in approvals through an SSH profile still held after the profile moved to another server. ([#4222](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4222)) - Publishing a connection to the team library uploaded its tunnel command and startup commands. ([#4222](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4222)) - Reset All Settings left iCloud password sync on until relaunch, though the Sync pane showed it off. ([#4222](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4222)) - A reconnect TablePro started on its own could follow an edited SSH profile to another server under an open window. ([#4222](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4222)) - Copied connection strings and MCP tokens were not marked concealed, so clipboard history apps could keep them. ([#4222](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4222)) - Always Allow was offered for a local link to a connection that goes through a proxy, tunnel command or SSH profile. ([#4222](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4222)) - Safe Mode missed a statement after a string glued to a name, such as `x$e'\\'` on PostgreSQL. ([#4236](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4236)) - On SQL databases the assistant's Edit mode ran schema, privilege, session and transaction statements, such as GRANT. ([#4244](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4244)) - Read-Only on iPhone and iPad ran a query that called a function which writes data. ([#4244](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4244)) - Safe Mode and MCP missed a PostgreSQL statement hidden after a `BEGIN ATOMIC` body that selects `begin atomic`. ([#4254](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4254)) - Read-Only blocks an Oracle or Dameng function called without parentheses, and a SurrealDB fn:: call. ([#4260](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4260)) - AI Edit mode refuses schema, privilege and session commands on MongoDB, Redis, Neo4j and every other engine. ([#4260](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4260)) - A Server Dashboard tile runs in the schema Read-Only checked, after any statement a query tab is running. ([#4262](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4262)) - AI Edit mode refuses writes into ScyllaDB's audit log and Kafka topics of Schema Registry, Connect or Streams. ([#4262](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4262)) - Replacing a Realtime Database top-level node, or an escaped Memcached flush_all, now counts as destructive. ([#4262](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4262))

# What's New in TablePro 0.87.0-beta.1
### Added
- PostgreSQL notices such as RAISE NOTICE show in the Output view, and a plan from EXPLAIN ANALYZE gains Output too. ([#4061](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4061)) - Export Results… has a keyboard shortcut, ⌥⇧⌘E, which you can change in Settings > Keyboard. ([#4066](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4066)) - tablepro completion prints a completion script for zsh, bash and fish. ([#4145](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4145)) - tablepro pair and tablepro unpair pair the command with TablePro or revoke its token. ([#4145](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4145)) - The tablepro command lists databases, schemas and tables, describes and exports tables, and reports its status. ([#4145](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4145)) - The get_table_health MCP tool returns Table Health findings to a connected client. ([#4167](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4167)) - Table Health checks redundant and invalid indexes, values near their limit, transaction ID age and stale statistics. ([#4167](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4167)) - Table Health finds reclaimable space on MySQL and MariaDB. ([#4167](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4167)) - Table Health marks new findings, keeps resolved ones and lets you ignore a finding, per database. ([#4167](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4167)) - Table Health exports findings to CSV, Excel, JSON and other formats, copies them, and saves every fix as one script. ([#4167](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4167))
### Changed
- On iOS, usage data goes to PostHog instead of TablePro's server, and only after you choose Share Usage Data. ([#4058](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4058)) - SQL passed to tablepro query that starts with a dash now goes after --. ([#4145](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4145)) - tablepro opens files and links in the TablePro it ships in, and a hidden connection exits 2 like an unknown one. ([#4145](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4145)) - tablepro exits 2 for a target that is neither a URL nor a file; open a file named like a command with tablepro open. ([#4145](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4145)) - With Reduce Transparency on, themes now color the sidebar and inspector on macOS 26 and later. ([#4153](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4153)) - Table Health opens one tab per database and stays on it when the sidebar switches database. ([#4167](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4167))
### Fixed
- Oracle output from a grid save, Commit or an AI statement showed under the next statement run from the editor. ([#4061](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4061)) - The Restore Previous Values toolbar button ignored a shortcut assigned to it in Settings > Keyboard. ([#4066](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4066)) - A database or schema's Export… in the sidebar showed ⇧⌘E, which exports the selected tables instead. ([#4066](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4066)) - tablepro query with TablePro closed could start another copy of TablePro, or the iPad app, and then time out. ([#4145](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4145)) - Settings offered a tablepro link line that broke once TablePro left its disk image. ([#4145](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4145)) - tablepro --help and tablepro --version opened TablePro instead of printing help or the version. ([#4145](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4145)) - Revoking an MCP token showed it as revoked even when TablePro could not save the change. ([#4145](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4145)) - Bars in the inspector lost their background under a theme on macOS 13 to 15. ([#4153](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4153)) - The license notice over Charts and Query Insights covered a themed window in system gray with Reduce Transparency on. ([#4153](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4153)) - Filter bar rows no longer center or drift out of line when a value is a pop-up, Between or Raw SQL. ([#4164](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4164)) - Table Health reported a PostgreSQL standby's activity counters and objects an extension owns. ([#4167](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4167)) - Saving a connection deleted its API token, TOTP secret or key passphrase when the Keychain could not be read. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Edits left on a background tab were reapplied to a different result that arrived while it was hidden. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - A DuckDB query over a very large result held every row in memory twice before showing the first page. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Items deleted on another Mac while their sync category was off stayed here and could come back everywhere. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Exporting an empty PostgreSQL table to CSV with field names wrote no header line. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Format Query put spaces around the @ of a MySQL account name or quoted user variable. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Saving, switching tabs during the Safe Mode prompt, then approving wiped the other tab's edits. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Deleting a row with unsaved edits could delete a different row, or none. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Editing a field inside an Elasticsearch object left the old value in the document beside the new one. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Editing a Redis string value in the grid removed the key's TTL. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Editing a string in an untyped SurrealDB field to text that looks like a number changed its type. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Renaming an etcd key or adding one overwrote an existing key, and a rename took two separate steps. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Adding an Elasticsearch row with an _id that exists replaced the existing document. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - A sidebar command on another database's table ran on the current database when the switch failed. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Redoing a cell edit on a row with another unsaved edit showed the value but never saved it. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Choosing Save on a second closing tab while the first was still saving left the first tab unclosable. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Copying a PostgreSQL text array into a JSON column wrote invalid JSON or turned strings into numbers. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - After a dropped connection reconnected, statements ran outside the transaction that was lost, with no error. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Rebuilding a SQLite table with a transaction open in the editor deleted its child rows. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Copy DDL and SQL export recreated a PostgreSQL partitioned or unlogged table as a plain table. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Renaming a Redis key or adding a string key overwrote an existing key of that name. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Editing a MySQL or MariaDB BIT cell saved the wrong value: 5 was stored as 53. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Cmd+Return right after typing in a very large script ran the text from before the last keystrokes. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - A save could fail on a unique constraint because edits ran before earlier deletes. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Query parameters mistook Snowflake paths, array slices or ClickHouse typed slots for :name parameters. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - A transaction opened in a tab on another PostgreSQL database was silently rolled back after a few minutes. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - A query approved in Safe Mode after switching tabs ran in the newly selected tab's database. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Shortcuts Add Rows inserted empty CSV cells as empty strings instead of NULL or the column default. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - One unreadable saved MCP token, or a failed keychain read, removed every paired client's token. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Format Query split PostgreSQL operators such as pgvector's <#> or pg_trgm's <%. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - XLSX export turned text such as 1E5 or Infinity into numbers and lost digits of long ids. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Pasting spreadsheet rows whose first cell is empty shifted every value one column left. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - CSV import silently dropped extra fields. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - A failed trigger edit could leave the trigger dropped with only a syntax error shown. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - An outside MCP server with long or dotted tool names made every chat request on its connections fail. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - A DuckDB export or table copy of more than 5,000,000 rows stopped at 5,000,000 and reported success. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Pasting or bulk-editing tens of thousands of rows froze the window for many seconds. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Reopening a closed connection from a deeplink or history replaced its saved tabs with one tab. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Keyword casing rewrote words inside string literals and in non-SQL editors such as MongoDB. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Stopping the assistant during a tool call broke the conversation; every later message failed. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Parquet export wrote NULL for values that did not fit the column type, with no warning. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Editing a MySQL or MariaDB trigger dropped it and ran its body as a statement. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - A long Snowflake statement was run a second time when the session expired while it ran. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Kafka topics and SurrealDB tables were browsed with a generic SQL SELECT instead of the driver's own query. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - A SQL dump of a MySQL BIT column restored different values than the table held. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Saving a password failed silently when the Keychain held both a synced and a local copy for the connection. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Running a query over an edited result discarded the unsaved edits without asking. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - A Snowflake statement still running after 45 minutes was reported as failed but kept running on the server. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - A structure save that failed part way on MySQL left edits staged that could not be saved again. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Parquet export wrote wrong bytes for binary values and NULL for an empty one. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - An error sent mid-stream by an OpenAI-compatible or Gemini provider ended the reply silently. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Editing a MongoDB string field to text that looks like a number or boolean changed its type. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - A write that outlasted the MCP or assistant timeout was reported as failed although it was applied. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Return and Delete on a selected row in the Welcome window, Favorites and the connections strip no longer do nothing. ([#4175](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4175)) - The host, attached database and extension lists in the connection form no longer hide the rows that do not fit. ([#4175](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4175)) - On macOS 27, clicking a row in a list or table no longer leaves its selection grey and the arrow keys going elsewhere. ([#4175](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4175)) - MySQL statements on iOS that ran past 30 seconds failed while the server kept running and committed them. ([#4177](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4177)) - Saving a password on iOS with Sync Passwords off deleted the iCloud Keychain copy your other devices use. ([#4177](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4177)) - Stop on iOS left a MySQL statement running on the server, which then committed it. ([#4177](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4177)) - Switching apps on iOS with a DuckDB transaction open rolled it back without any message. ([#4177](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4177)) - A password saved on iOS while Sync Passwords was off went unused once Sync Passwords was turned back on. ([#4177](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4177)) - A PostgreSQL query on iOS hung for about two hours when the network dropped its reply. ([#4177](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4177)) - A password saved while Sync Passwords was off went unused once Sync Passwords was turned back on. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - Items deleted on another Mac came back after iCloud sync had to download everything again. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - Saving a connection rewrote passwords you did not change, overwriting a newer one saved on another device. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - Editing a SurrealDB field that held both strings and numbers changed the edited value's type. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - Claude Agent asked for MCP access to the chat's connection on every message at Ask Once. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - Pasting spreadsheet rows with empty cells wrote NULL instead of the column's default value. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - Switching databases on a connection that reconnects to switch rolled back an open transaction without asking. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - Saving, closing or switching tabs right after typing in a very large script lost the last keystrokes. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - A structure save or column reorder that failed part way did not say which changes were already applied. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - Importing, copying or syncing rows into a MySQL or MariaDB BIT column stored the wrong value: 5 became 53. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - Adding a Redis hash, list, set or sorted set key in the grid wrote into an existing key of that name. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - Reading a SQLite full-text search table over MCP or from the assistant failed with authorization denied. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - A MySQL or MariaDB query with no query timeout hung for about two hours when the network dropped its reply. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - Text over 4 KB in a SQL Server, Oracle or DuckDB table on iOS could not be loaded in full, edited or copied. ([#4179](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4179)) - A large MySQL or SQL Server query on iOS kept downloading every remaining row after the row cap was reached. ([#4179](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4179)) - The query timeout on iOS was ignored on PostgreSQL, Redshift and Oracle, and as a lock timeout on SQL Server. ([#4179](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4179)) - A MySQL result on iOS that exactly filled the row cap said more rows were left out. ([#4179](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4179)) - After a low-memory trim on iOS, the data browser's page range named rows it no longer showed. ([#4179](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4179))
### Security
- tablepro export printed control codes stored in the database to the terminal, where they could run. ([#4145](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4145)) - The tablepro command and the MCP bridge could send their token to a program that replaced TablePro's socket. ([#4145](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4145)) - MCP argument completion listed a connection's databases and tables to a client that was not approved for it. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Deleting the connections.json tag file let an edited connection list run its password and tunnel commands. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - A Local only connection's newly saved passwords and keys still synced through iCloud Keychain. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - Claude Agent could reach every saved connection through MCP instead of only the one the chat is on. ([#4174](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4174)) - MCP clients and the AI assistant could read masked values through a renamed column, a query plan or an error message. ([#4178](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4178)) - When the saved SSH host keys could not be read, a server whose key had changed was offered as a new server to trust. ([#4179](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4179))
[View release notes](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/releases/tag/v0.87.0-beta.1)

# What's New in TablePro 0.86.0
Sign in with a TablePro account to use your plan, see your devices and sync a team library. A license key from an earlier version moves into your account the first time the app opens.
A dropped connection keeps its rows while it reconnects, with Cancel, and every surface shows the same connection state.
Imports, exports, backups, restores and transfers share one progress sheet, and Quit, Close and Disconnect ask once about work still running.
Remote DuckDB connections can go through an SSH tunnel, Cloudflare Tunnel, SOCKS proxy or tunnel command, and now require the Token instead of secrets in ~/.duckdb.
A raw SQL filter can no longer run a second statement, and a DuckDB token no longer reaches another server that a later ATTACH names.
Sending feedback from inside the app is no longer available.
[View full changelog](https://docs.tablepro.app/changelog)

# What's New in TablePro 0.86.0-beta.1
### Added
- A dropped connection keeps its rows and shows a reconnecting bar with Cancel, then Reconnect after 10 tries. ([#4001](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4001)) - Settings > MCP offers Try Again when the server fails to start, and says when the port you set was in use. ([#4007](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4007)) - Linked folders show what each scan found, and Settings > License > Team shows the team library's last refresh. ([#4009](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4009)) - Downloading cloud-sql-proxy shows its progress with Cancel, and connecting says when it downloads. ([#4009](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4009)) - Quit, Close and Disconnect ask once, in one alert listing the restores, imports, exports and queries still running. ([#4009](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4009)) - A notification when an agent session waits for your answer or its reply fails while you are elsewhere. ([#4009](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4009)) - Plugin installs and updates show their progress with Cancel, and a failed update stays in Settings with Try Again. ([#4009](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4009)) - Remote DuckDB connections can go through an SSH tunnel, Cloudflare Tunnel, SOCKS proxy or tunnel command. ([#4021](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4021)) - Sign in with a TablePro account to unlock paid features, see your devices and sync a team library. ([#4045](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4045))
### Changed
- The connections strip, Welcome, the switcher, menus and the iOS app show one connection state, only when it needs you. ([#4001](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4001)) - The welcome window shows a license that needs attention and iCloud sync problems, each linking to the fix. ([#4005](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4005)) - Notices, warnings and errors use the standard macOS look: color only on the symbol, with no tinted boxes, dots or chips. ([#4007](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4007)) - Connection tags are edited in a token field: type a name to add or create a tag, and press Delete to remove one. ([#4007](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4007)) - Plugins that could not load are listed in Settings > Extensions with the reason, Update, Try Again and Remove. ([#4007](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4007)) - On iOS, a saved row no longer shows a toast, and NULL, Default and column types use standard buttons and text. ([#4007](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4007)) - A finished tab shows a checkmark and a failed one a red triangle, where both showed the same dot. ([#4009](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4009)) - Imports, exports, backups, restores, transfers and copies share one progress sheet, and Escape asks before stopping. ([#4009](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4009)) - The MCP disconnect tool refuses while the connection has running work, unsaved changes or an open transaction. ([#4018](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4018)) - Remote DuckDB connections now require the Token and no longer read secrets saved in ~/.duckdb. ([#4021](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4021)) - etcd keys and values that are not UTF-8 show as hex, and a quoted `\xHH` in an etcd command writes that byte. ([#4023](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4023)) - A license key from an earlier version moves into your TablePro account the first time the app opens. ([#4045](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4045))
### Removed
- Sending feedback from inside the app is no longer available. ([#4045](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4045))
### Fixed
- A failed connect showed as disconnected on the connections strip, and a lost connection as failed. ([#4001](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4001)) - On iOS, a lost connection stopped reconnecting after one failed try. ([#4001](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4001)) - The toolbar lost the connection's name after a disconnect. ([#4001](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4001)) - Cancelling a reconnect after an SSH tunnel dropped did not stop it, and the connection could come back on its own. ([#4001](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4001)) - Try Again on a license check showed nothing when the check failed. ([#4005](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4005)) - Pro features asked a license that could not be checked for 30 days, or was suspended, to buy a license. ([#4005](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4005)) - Sync Now showed for iCloud problems that trying again cannot clear, such as a restricted account. ([#4005](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4005)) - The MCP status said the port was in use whenever the failure text happened to contain 48. ([#4007](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4007)) - Notes from MySQL and SQLite maintenance, such as an OPTIMIZE note or an integrity check problem, were never shown. ([#4007](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4007)) - Settings > Notifications kept showing an old permission after it was changed in System Settings. ([#4007](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4007)) - A GitHub Copilot error showed only inside its provider sheet while the provider row said Not signed in. ([#4007](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4007)) - A restore's progress bar never moved. ([#4009](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4009)) - A team library pull kept connection settings it should have removed until TablePro restarted. ([#4009](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4009)) - Restores, comparisons and sync scripts never notified when they finished out of sight. ([#4009](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4009)) - Quitting left a restore or backup tool running in the background. ([#4009](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4009)) - Importing from another app now keeps the TLS, key passphrases and extra connection files that app saved. ([#4015](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4015)) - Restore Previous Values stayed enabled with nothing to restore, then only showed an alert. ([#4018](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4018)) - The selected connection in the sidebar showed a blank white badge when it was lost or failed. ([#4018](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4018)) - An export or table transfer kept running with no window after a disconnect that did not ask first. ([#4018](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4018)) - On iOS, the NULL button moved across the field when turned on while editing a row. ([#4018](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4018)) - Raw filter rows were offered on etcd, DynamoDB, Memcached, Weaviate, InfluxDB and Kafka, which cannot run them. ([#4019](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4019)) - Loading a filter preset turned its same element rows into any element rows. ([#4019](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4019)) - Raw SQL filters on SQL Server and Oracle failed with an invalid column error. ([#4019](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4019)) - Changing a filter's operator kept the old Match Case setting, and Search All Rows matched case. ([#4019](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4019)) - Duplicate Filter dropped Match Case and the element scope, and put the cursor in the wrong row. ([#4019](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4019)) - The cell Filter menu added a second copy of a filter that was already running. ([#4019](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4019)) - Switching a filter row between Raw SQL and a column hid the text you had typed. ([#4019](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4019)) - A page turn, sort or refresh ran filter edits that had not been applied. ([#4019](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4019)) - A filter that could not run, such as raw SQL with a comment, loaded every row while showing as applied. ([#4019](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4019)) - MongoDB exports cut nested values at 10,000 characters. ([#4020](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4020)) - MQL exports lost special field names and changed numeric field order. ([#4020](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4020)) - MQL exports lost empty collections and skipped some index and validator values. ([#4020](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4020)) - MQL exports changed mixed-type fields, nested BSON values and stored nulls. ([#4020](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4020)) - Drop offered to ignore foreign key checks on DuckDB, ClickHouse, SQL Server, SurrealDB, Teradata and Beancount. ([#4021](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4021)) - A remote DuckDB connection that could not download the Quack extension showed a misleading error. ([#4021](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4021)) - Remote DuckDB connections ignored the SSL settings shown and could not trust a private CA or self-signed certificate. ([#4021](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4021)) - Beancount and Memcached showed Database instead of Ledger or Server once their driver loaded. ([#4021](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4021)) - A copied connection URL misread IPv6 hosts and dropped the settings after a database name holding # or ?. ([#4021](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4021)) - Saving an etcd key that ends in a zero width space or starts with a byte order mark changed a different key. ([#4023](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4023)) - etcd `get`, `del` and `watch` with `--prefix` could reach keys outside the prefix when it ended in some non-ASCII text. ([#4023](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4023)) - etcd `get "" --prefix`, and exporting the root of a connection with no key prefix, failed with "key is not provided". ([#4023](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4023)) - Editing or deleting a non-UTF-8 etcd key changed a key named `<b64:…>`, and a rename saved a binary value as text. ([#4023](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4023)) - etcd keys starting with `--` could not be saved or deleted from the grid. ([#4023](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4023)) - etcd commands could run without the read-only or delete limits set by the app. ([#4023](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4023)) - An etcd range query with invalid page bounds could crash the app. ([#4023](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4023)) - SQLite, libSQL, DuckDB and Beancount cut text at a NUL character when reading or saving it. ([#4024](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4024)) - MongoDB edits and deletes could target the wrong document after reconnecting or switching databases. ([#4028](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4028)) - MCP and AI chat could not confirm a DELETE without WHERE, leaving it blocked or routed through the wrong tool. ([#4029](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4029)) - Stopping an import could misreport rollback, and opening another dialog could hide a running transfer. ([#4031](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4031)) - The iPad app on a Mac crashing when you open a connection, or add or edit one. ([#4032](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4032)) - Data dictionary exports could render names and comments as markup when Unicode characters joined punctuation. ([#4034](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4034)) - SQL Server edits could target the wrong text key, and filters or SQL exports could change Unicode or line endings. ([#4035](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4035)) - SQL Server edits on a char or varchar key could also change a row whose key differs only by characters like ß and ss. ([#4039](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4039)) - Deleting or editing a Firebase node or collection whose name starts with a combining mark changed the name without it. ([#4040](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4040)) - Editing or deleting a Databend row whose text held a NUL before digits could change a different row. ([#4041](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4041)) - A Databend table with a backtick in its name opened, edited and exported as another table. ([#4041](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4041)) - A value bound into a Databend query behind some comments or hints could land outside its quotes. ([#4041](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4041)) - Read-Only and Safe Mode treated pg_background, pg_cron and TimescaleDB calls, drop_chunks included, as reads. ([#4043](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4043)) - Safe Mode on Databend missed a DROP or other write hidden behind an optimizer hint, a comment or SETTINGS. ([#4044](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4044)) - A StarRocks query parameter stored a form feed as the letter f, or failed after a comment ending in a carriage return. ([#4044](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4044))
### Security
- A raw SQL filter could close its own parentheses and run a second statement, such as a DELETE. ([#4019](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4019)) - A remote DuckDB token could reach another Quack server that a later ATTACH in the same session named. ([#4021](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/pull/4021))
[View release notes](https://github.com/TableProApp/TablePro/releases/tag/v0.86.0-beta.1)

# What's New in TablePro 0.85.0
Neo4j, InfluxDB 2 and 3, Qdrant, Memcached and StarRocks connections, and KingbaseES with a downloadable driver.
Two to six query results show as tabs, and the Structure tab shows columns, indexes, foreign keys and checks on one page.
Masking rules hide column values in the grid, copies, exports, the AI assistant and MCP. Table Health finds bloat and unused indexes.
Routine Debugger steps through PL/pgSQL and PL/SQL, and Live Messages watches PostgreSQL notifications, Redis channels and Kafka topics.
Imported and synced connections ask before using cloud or Kerberos sign-ins, and PostgreSQL reads ~/.pgpass only when you turn it on.
Settings > Plugins is now Settings > Extensions. A .sql-formatter.json saved by 0.83 needs exporting again with sql-formatter's key names.
[View full changelog](https://docs.tablepro.app/changelog)

# What's New in TablePro 0.84.0
Find and Replace work in every data grid, with Match Case, Whole Words, regular expressions and a column scope.
Click a sorted header to reverse it or Option-click to add a sort key. Frozen columns sort, resize and reorder from their own headers.
A cell value with a line break or over 256 characters opens in an editor anchored to the cell.
The sidebar, Open Quickly, autocomplete and AI chat no longer stall on databases with tens of thousands of tables.
Procedures and Functions load on MySQL 5.x and MariaDB servers with many routines, and MariaDB packages open.
Save Changes has its own toolbar section, and panes switch views with native tabs.
[View full changelog](https://docs.tablepro.app/changelog)
